Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

Article Title: 'Want to see who modified Form 6': SC refuses to pass interim order to suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:
SC on Monday heard two pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

What did the petitioners seek?

What is the EC SIR row?

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to pass an interim order seeking the suspension of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and issued notice to the Election Commission of India, CEC and the other two election commissioners on a plea challenging decisions taken by the poll body on Special Intensive Revision.A bench led by CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard pleas filed by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi. The pleas raised questions over whether Gyanesh used powers belonging to the Election Commission without the approval of election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.“Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When record has produced, we would like to see who has modified. But, your prayers appear jumbled up,” the CJI noted.The apex court directed the respondents to file their responses to the allegations. The court said it would examine whether the statutory scheme was followed and indicated that if the records showed that any decision was not taken in accordance with the law, it could injunct such a decision and hold it ultra vires."If records show some decision was not unanimous etc., we will injunct those decisions and say they are ultra-vires.Can we ex-parte come to decision that all decisions were unilateral? We expect them to respond in a clear, transparent manner," Justice Bagchi added.One of the plea sought Gyanesh's suspension until the final hearing to protect the “multi-member character of the Election Commission”. It asked that Sandhu and Joshi run the commission's business together in the meantime and that any vacancy be filled on the recommendation of a committee that includes the Chief Justice of India.However, the second plea sought criminal proceedings against the CEC and other officials for allegedly failing in their official duty. It further sought a declaration that all decisions, guidelines and software changes made under Gyanesh without the full commission's agreement are “unconstitutional, ultra vires and void ab initio”, meaning illegal and invalid from the start.Tripathi's plea relies on Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, which says the majority view prevails when commissioners differ. The plea argued that the law requires decisions to be taken together.A report by the Indian Express claimed that commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders relating to the SIR, which were allegedly issued without their knowledge or recommendation.On Form 6, the voter registration form, the plea alleges that a requirement for ancestral details and a link to the previous SIR was added through the poll panel's software without the legal amendment the election rules require. It claims the other two commissioners objected to the change.On Goa, it alleges that the software lacked a feature to restore 97 eligible voters despite directions to verify them.On West Bengal, it claims more than 16.10 lakh appeals were filed in the EC's name against voters whose names were restored by judicial officers. It says the other two commissioners and the state's chief electoral officer did not know about these appeals or approve them.The Election Commission has said differing views are a normal part of discussions in any institution and that all its orders are legally valid and follow the set procedures.
Article Summary: Supreme Court on Monday refused to pass an interim order seeking the suspension of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. A bench led by CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard pleas filed by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi. The pleas raised questions over whether CEC used powers belonging to the Election Commission without approval.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

-

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: 'Look Out Circular' against parents of man who secretly took away child to US
Article Text:
SC said that all attempts were being made by the man’s parents to surreptitiously leave the country and obstruct the course of justice

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It is increasingly becoming common in matrimonial disputes involving NRI couples, particularly child custody cases, for one spouse to take the child to a foreign country where he or she works and refuse to submit to the jurisdiction of Indian courts, leaving the other partner behind. Now, Supreme Court has indicated that in such cases, the parents of the runaway partner have to face the consequences.Hearing such a case, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan revived a 'Look Out Circular' - monitor, trace, or restrict travel of individuals - against the parents of a man who clandestinely took away his three-and-a-half-year-old daughter to the US, without informing his wife, and has refused to bring her back to India."The minor child, at the relevant point of time, aged three-and-a-half years, was taken away by the father to US. The mother is relentlessly trying to get her daughter back. The mother is in a pathetic condition. We have no idea in what circumstances the minor daughter is residing in US with her father, that too a working father," the bench said.It added that all attempts are being made by the man's parents to surreptitiously leave this country and obstruct the course of justice."We have stayed the operation of the order passed by Madras High Court setting aside the Look Out Circular," the bench said.It granted the man a last chance to come back to India with the minor child. "We have made ourselves more than clear that he has to come to India within four weeks from the US with her, failing which his parents will have to face severe legal consequences. We have made the parents understand in vernacular," Supreme Court said.The bench said that if he was not inclined to come to India within four weeks, then he should make necessary arrangements to put the child on board along with an escort. It also asked him to hand over the child to the mother if she reached US."We have passed this order keeping in mind the interest of the child, who was taken-away by her father deceitfully when she was just three-and-a-half years of age. Why should she be deprived of the love, care and affection of her own mother? Why should he stay back in US along with the daughter?" the court said in its order and posted the hearing after a month.
Article Summary: A man clandestinely took away his three-and-a-half-year-old daughter to the US, without informing his wife, and has refused to bring her back to India. Supreme Court has indicated that in such cases, the parents of the runaway partner have to face the consequences.

Article Title: Kashmiri teacher fights period stigma, one village at a time
Article Text:

BARAMULLA: While most schools are quiet on Sundays, Aasima Jan heads into north Kashmir’s remote tribal villages to talk to girls and families about a subject many still avoid: menstruation. For years, the 42-year-old govt school teacher has conducted awareness sessions on menstrual health, hygiene and stigma, while also persuading families to re-enrol children who have dropped out of school. Her efforts earned her J&K’s “Best Teacher Award” in 2023.Recruited in 2003, Aasima spent seven years teaching at a govt school in Bandipora. In 2009, she noticed many girls missing classes for up to a week during their periods. Some said their parents barred them from attending school while menstruating.The turning point came when she found a student crying over the shame surrounding periods. “It broke my heart. I felt a deep sense of responsibility and resolved to do something about it,” Aasima said. The next day, she began taking extra classes on menstruation and started counselling parents. “I tell girls this is natural. It is not a disease, but a sign that they are growing up,” she said.Attendance among girls improved.Aasima then moved beyond the classroom, conducting monthly awareness sessions at schools and visiting villages on Sundays and holidays. She continued the sessions even after her transfer to neighbouring Baramulla district. Her outreach expanded to remote areas such as Gurez and Uri, and to nomadic Gujjar and Bakerwal communities.Every Sunday, she picks a village, contacts local panches and sarpanches, and conducts sessions centred on “awareness, acceptance and action”. In remote areas, she often finds girls using cloth during periods while families, including mothers, are reluctant to discuss menstruation. Aasima spends her own money buying sanitary pads to distribute during visits, while explaining their use and disposal.Her social media page, with around 40,000 followers, also promotes menstrual health and other social causes. For Aasima, the biggest reward is seeing students continue the work by spreading awareness and positivity about menstrual health.
Article Summary: Aasima Jan is a govt school teacher in north Kashmir. She has conducted awareness sessions on menstrual health, hygiene and stigma. Her efforts earned her J&K’s ‘Best Teacher Award’ in 2023. “I tell girls this is natural. It is not a disease, but a sign that they are growing up,” she said.

Article Title: Singeetham Srinivasa Rao: Seven decades, many worlds of cinema
Article Text:

BENGALURU: Singeetham Srinivasa Rao , who died in Chennai on Saturday aged 95, had a career that spanned more than seven decades of Indian cinema . He entered films in 1954 as an apprentice to legendary Telugu filmmaker KV Reddy, assisting him on Donga Ramudu and Mayabazar.From those early days on the sets of a Telugu classic, Rao went on to become one of Indian cinema’s most inventive filmmakers, leaving a particularly rich mark on Kannada cinema while also making acclaimed films in Tamil, Telugu and other languages.His Kannada journey began before he became a director. Rao was the executive director of Samskara (1970), Pattabhirama Reddy’s landmark adaptation of UR Ananthamurthy’s novel. The film, which won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film, became a defining work of Kannada parallel cinema. It was an early indication of the range of a filmmaker who would later move comfortably between art-house cinema and popular entertainment.His directorial debut in Kannada came with Rajkumar in Haalu Jenu in 1982. What followed was one of the notable actor-director collaborations in Kannada cinema, with Chalisuva Modagalu, Eradu Nakshatragalu, Shravana Banthu, Jwaalamukhi, Bhagyada Lakshmi Baramma and Devatha Manushya — all after Gogak Chaluvali.The films moved across family drama, romance, crime and comedy, with Rao adapting his craft to each. Devatha Manushya was also Rajkumar’s 200th film.His association with the Rajkumar family extended beyond the thespian himself. In Anand (1986), Rao introduced Shivarajkumar as a leading man. He later directed Raghavendra Rajkumar in Chiranjeevi Sudhakar. His association with the Rajkumar banner also included work on other films produced by the family.There was another side to Rao’s Kannada work that is less often remembered: music. A disciple of composer S Rajeswara Rao, he also composed music, giving Kannada cinema some memorable albums. He composed the songs and score for Bhagyada Lakshmi Baramma and the songs for Samyuktha, moving between direction and music with the same ease with which he moved between genres.Then came Pushpaka Vimana (1987), the dialogue-free film starring Kamal Haasan. The movie, which became one of the most distinctive films of its time, was another example of Rao refusing to be confined by conventional cinematic language. Though often remembered primarily through its Tamil connection, it was produced as a Kannada entry and won the National Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment.His apprenticeship under KV Reddy had taken him through some of Telugu cinema’s landmark films. Decades later, he returned to Telugu cinema as a director with films such as Aditya 369 and Bhairava Dweepam. In Tamil, his collaborations with Kamal Haasan produced films including Raja Paarvai, Apoorva Sagodharargal and Michael Madana Kama Rajan. His work also extended to Hindi, Malayalam and English.Across more than seven decades, Rao’s filmography was less a straight line than a series of departures. He began as a young apprentice learning from KV Reddy on films such as Mayabazar, became part of the Kannada New Wave through Samskara, worked extensively with Rajkumar, introduced two of his sons, experimented with a dialogue-free film and continued moving between languages and genres almost until the end.
Article Summary: Singeetham Srinivasa Rao had a career that spanned more than seven decades of Indian cinema. He entered films in 1954 as an apprentice to legendary Telugu filmmaker KV Reddy. He left a particularly rich mark on Kannada cinema while also making acclaimed films in Tamil, Telugu and other languages.

Article Title: 'Equal share and equal respect': Congress's reply to Akhilesh's seat-sharing pitch
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh Congress in charge Rajendra Pal Gautam on Sunday demanded "equal share and equal respect" for his party amid the ongoing tussle with alliance partner Samajwadi Party over seat sharing for the upcoming assembly polls in the state.Gautam said that both Congress and SP must move forward together and asserted that both parties should settle the seat sharing issue in October."I have been saying from the beginning that there should be equal respect and an equal share. After all, Congress is the country’s oldest and largest party. Congress fought the freedom movement and represents the idea of India," Gautam told news agency ANI."As far as seat-sharing is concerned, I have been saying from the beginning that we should settle the seat-sharing issue completely in the month of October so that every person who is contesting, or will contest, gets enough time to work in their constituency," he added.The remarks came after Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said that the larger objective of the alliance should be electoral victory rather than which party is getting how many seats.In a post on X, Akhilesh said that when the objective is clear and alliance partners work together, the journey towards the goal becomes easier."When the goal is clear, hand in hand we stand; when the gaze is fixed on the destination, the journey becomes easy! The big thing isn't how many seats the alliance gets or which seat goes to whom - the big thing is that we all must ensure that the victory belongs to the alliance," Akhilesh said."Let us repeat again: It's not about the seats, it's about the victory," he added.The SP chief said the proposed alliance victory would be larger than the interests of individual parties and linked the effort to issues including communalism, democracy, the Constitution, reservations and social harmony."This victory will be greater than the parties in our alliance - it will be the victory of all of us, of that united effort that persists in struggle so that communalism may never raise its head again, so that BJP's influence may not touch democracy, the Constitution, or reservations, and so that the country's harmony may bloom once more, and the nation's progress and prosperity may smile again," he said.Uttar Pradesh is heading for assembly polls in 2027.In the 2022 assembly polls, BJP retained power by winning 255 of the 403 constituencies, securing a 41.29 per cent vote share.Former CM Akhilesh Yadav-led Samajwadi Party came a distant second in the 2022 election, securing 111 seats and getting 32.06 per cent of the votes.Meanwhile, SP and Congress fought the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh as allies under the INDIA bloc.The Samajwadi Party (SP) won 37 seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, emerging as the single-largest party in Uttar Pradesh and the third-largest party overall in the 18th Lok Sabha. Congress holds six of the 80 Lok Sabha seats.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh Congress in charge Rajendra Pal Gautam demanded "equal share and equal respect" for his party amid the ongoing tussle with alliance partner Samajwadi Party over seat sharing for the upcoming assembly polls in the state. The remarks came after Akhilesh Yadav said that the larger objective of the alliance should be electoral victory.

Article Title: No whataboutery can justify voter disenfranchisement, says SC judge; oppn says CEC 'exposed'

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process that "disenfranchises millions of Indian citizens" is “intrinsically arbitrary” and a negation of the constitutional order. The remarks were then cited by opposition leaders to target Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India,” Bar and Bench quoted Justice Bhuyan as saying.He said the Constitution does not create two classes of citizens based on voting rights and added that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 326 and 14.“No authority can do it; no court can condone it. No one is above the Constitution,” he said.On deletion of names from electoral rolls, Bhuyan said, “Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing.From the persona of an Indian citizen, the right to vote or right to be included in the voters list cannot be detached. It will be like taking out the soul from the body.”Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said Bhuyan’s remarks showed that the CEC had violated the Constitution “both in letter and spirit”. “Justice Bhuyan has said much more and has exposed the CEC lock, stock and barrel. Gyanesh Kumar simply has lost all moral right to continue in office,” Ramesh said."Justice Ujjal Bhuyan, a sitting judge of the Supreme Court, has been an outspoken champion of environmental protection. Now the courageous jurist has forcefully expressed his view that the right to vote is very much part of the basic structure of the Constitution. This conclusively proves that the CEC—Constitutional functionary himself—has violated the Constitution itself both in letter and spirit," he said."Justice Bhuyan has said much more and has exposed the CEC lock, stock and barrel. Gyanesh Kumar simply has lost all moral right to continue in office," he added.TMC MP Mahua Moitra also praised Bhuyan, saying, “It’s easy for a judge to grow a spine the day he retires. It’s a first when a sitting judge speaks truth to power. Kudos to Justice Bhuyan.”
Article Summary: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process that "disenfranchises millions of Indian citizens" is “intrinsically arbitrary” and a negation of the constitutional order. The remarks were then cited by opposition leaders to target Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Article Title: India can launch surgical strikes on Pakistan, but can't hold talks: Mani Shankar Aiyar

SRINAGAR: Former Union minister Mani Shankar Aiyar criticised the BJP-led central government for refusing to hold talks with Pakistan, saying it has the "courage" to launch surgical strikes but lacks the willingness to resolve issues.Speaking at the 5th Halla Bolle Conclave here, the Congress veteran suggested holding talks at the Attari-Wagah border, asserting that arguing over past issues was not foreign policy."We seem to have the courage to go into surgical strikes with them. Why don't we have the courage to sit across the table with them? Why can't we talk to them? Why can't we make friends with them?" he asked."Is there any other country in the world with whom we are more comfortable than with Pakistan? Is there any country in the world with whom Pakistan is more able to, you know, chat than with us?" he asked.Pointing to previous dialogue processes with Pakistan, Aiyar asked, "Why don't we show the courage to go there, and let them come here?""And if you don't have that courage, then my suggestion is that we meet at Wagah-Attari. Place a table right on our border line so that the Pakistani delegation doesn't leave Pakistan to talk to us, and we don't leave India to talk to them. And keep this dialogue going," he said.He said the dialogue can establish what can be resolved and what cannot be resolved."Wherever a resolution emerges, let us take action on that. And whatever hasn't been resolved, just postpone it, saying that for now it seems we cannot agree on this, but we will continue our dialogue. And whenever the atmosphere changes, then we will take up these remaining issues as well," he added.He, however, asserted that having arguments about the past was not foreign affairs."I think the only way we can arrive at any kind of constructive conclusion is by talking to them, however long it takes. And that is what the Americans did with the Russians. They never broke the diplomatic relationship; they never broke the dialogue. Sensible countries talk to each other; stupid countries don't talk to each other," he said.To a question about the political situation in the country, Aiyar said, 'It is very easy to fix what is wrong with the Indian political environment.""And to do that, you only have to follow the advice given by (PDP president) Mehbooba Mufti to Kashmiris, where she said that until all Kashmiris get together with a single voice, Delhi will not be influenced by individual Kashmiri leaders coming to Delhi," he said.The former Union minister added that the same can be said about the national political scene, which can be fixed when the entire non-Hindutva polity comes together."It can come together because we already have the INDIA bloc. And if the INDIA bloc comes together, we showed in the 2024 election that had we consolidated that bloc, we would have easily got the extra eight seats that are required to bring about a majority. And do you think Nitish would have joined him? Do you think Chandrababu would have joined him? No," he said."We would have been in Delhi, and Kashmir would have got back its statehood. Kashmir might even have received back Article 370 and 35A, perhaps in a slightly different shape. But if you want to make progress, those who disagree have to get together. And if we get together, then we can make new initiatives on Pakistan," he added.He emphasised that the Indian tradition is to talk."We need to talk to Srinagar, Srinagar needs to talk to Jammu, the street's voice needs to be brought into the discussion between the Government of India and the Government of Pakistan," he said.
Article Summary: Mani Shankar Aiyar criticises central government for refusing to hold talks with Pakistan. Suggests holding talks at the Attari-Wagah border, asserting that arguing over past issues was not foreign policy. Says dialogue can establish what can be resolved and what cannot be resolved.

Article Title: Jorge Jesus on Ronaldo row: 'You can’t break up a year-long friendship over a situation I can’t even understand… I don’t apologise to anyone'

Portugal's head coach Jorge Jesus speaks during a news conference in Copenhagen, Denmark, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026, ahead of their Nations League soccer match against Denmark. (Liselotte Sabroe/Ritzau Scanpix via AP)

Jorge Jesus has finally given his full account of the Cristiano Ronaldo controversy, and his latest comments have done little to cool the situation around Portugal. Rather than offering the apology Ronaldo was reportedly expecting, Jesus defended his decision, backed Bruno Fernandes' description of Ronaldo as the country's greatest icon and made clear that selecting the team remains entirely his responsibility.Speaking after Portugal's 2–1 Nations League victory over Norway on Sunday, Jesus addressed the dispute that began when Ronaldo left the national team camp following their previous meeting.“I don’t know what Cristiano may decide,” Jesus said. “I’ve already said what I had to say. For me, this was never an issue.”Jesus insisted that having Ronaldo as a national symbol did not mean he could not make footballing decisions involving the 41-year-old forward, particularly when he believed another choice was better for the team.“Having a player who is a symbol like him does not mean there has to be anything non-negotiable on my part as a coach. Nothing happened that called my authority into question.”Jesus also said Ronaldo remained eligible for selection in the next international window, provided he continues playing and chooses to return, while describing their relationship as one that should not be damaged permanently by what he considers a minor footballing incident.“For me, Cristiano will be eligible for selection the next time the squad is announced, provided he is playing. If he wants to, he will return to the national team. You can’t break up a year-long friendship because of a situation I can’t even understand.”Bruno Fernandes had already spoken publicly in defence of Ronaldo, insisting that his former Manchester United teammate remains the biggest figure in Portuguese football and calling for the squad to stay united.“I spoke with Cristiano and told him that he is and will always remain the GREATEST icon of our national team and our country. Our national team is united, not divided. Matters must be resolved internally and conclude well for both parties,” Fernandes said.Jesus said he completely agreed with that assessment, while revealing that he had previously spoken directly to Ronaldo about how he should view the later stages of his international career.“I completely agree with what Bruno Fernandes said. That is also my view. One of the things I told Cristiano was that he could not end his national-team career after losing at the World Cup and walking off in tears.”Jesus then returned to the decision that triggered the entire dispute and rejected the idea that he owed Ronaldo an apology for keeping him on the bench.“He was supposed to play here today, but, given everything that happened, the situation changed. Everything has been said. I am the head coach, I select whoever I want, and I don’t ask anyone who I should select or who should play.”“It was because the player had been warming up. Now, apologise for what and to whom? I don’t apologise to anyone,”he added, as per Flash Score. The dispute began when Jesus sent Ronaldo to warm up for around 30 minutes during Portugal's 2–1 Nations League victory over Norway before ultimately deciding not to use him.The decision led to an emergency meeting involving Ronaldo, Jesus and Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proença, but Ronaldo subsequently left the national team camp and said he would explain the reasons for his departure “in time”.Ronaldo wrote: “After the press conference of the national team and following a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.”He added: “In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave.”Jesus had promised to explain his side after Portugal's next match against Norway, and he has now done so, making clear that he accepts no wrongdoing over the decision while leaving the door open for Ronaldo to return.
Article Summary: Jorge Jesus has given his full account of the Cristiano Ronaldo controversy. Portugal head coach says Ronaldo can return to the national team. How separate are these operations? What safeguards are in place?” Cohn said. “Who inside Excel Search and Advisory has access to information about these candidates, and who doesn’t, for that matter? Is there a firewall between the executive search business and the agents representing WNBA players? … These are questions that need answers.”The concern is about the process, not a claim that Excel has acted improperly. Article Title: Nobel Prize in Medicine 2026: Trio win for breakthrough in optogenetics, unlocking how brain forms memories
Article Text:
Winner of Nobel Prize in Physiology or medicine (Credit: Mattias Karlén © The Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet)

Karl Deisseroth

Peter Hegemann

Georg Nagel

The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded on Monday to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel "for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics”, a technique that allows scientists to control the activity of nerve cells using light.The Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet said the three scientists had laid “the foundation of a new era in neuroscience”. Their work has enabled researchers to switch individual nerve cells on or off in living brains, helping them study how neural circuits control memories, feelings and behaviours.Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel discovered channelrhodopsin-1 and channelrhodopsin-2, a light-sensitive protein found in the single-celled alga Chlamydomonas. When exposed to blue light, the protein opens a channel through the cell membrane, allowing positively charged ions to flow in and generate an electrical signal.Karl Deisseroth later transformed this discovery into a tool for controlling nerve cells. In 2005, his research group introduced the gene for channelrhodopsin-2 into rat nerve cells grown in the laboratory. When exposed to blue light, the cells generated nerve signals.In 2007, Deisseroth and his team demonstrated that the technique could be used to control nerve cells in the brains of living mice.The method, which came to be known as optogenetics, has since become a widely used tool in neuroscience. Researchers have used it to identify neural circuits involved in functions including pain, social behaviour, thirst, food consumption, reward and attention, as well as to investigate neurological and psychiatric disorders.“Optogenetics provides opportunities for mapping the brain in a way that we could once only dream of,” Per Svenningsson, chair of the Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine, said.The work has also opened possible medical applications. Researchers are studying optogenetic approaches to restore vision in people with severe visual impairment, while the technique is also being investigated as a way to improve the precision of cochlear implants.Here is more info about the winners:Karl Deisseroth, born in Boston in 1971, is affiliated with the Howard Hughes Medical Institute and Stanford University in the US. He is the DH Chen Professor and a professor of bioengineering and psychiatry and behavioural sciences at Stanford.Deisseroth received his PhD from Stanford University in 1998 and his MD in 2000. His work has focused on developing tools to understand how specific nerve cells and neural circuits function in the living brain.Peter Hegemann, born in Münster, Germany, in 1954, is the Hertie Senior Professor of Neuroscience at Humboldt University of Berlin. He received his PhD from the Max Planck Institute for Biochemistry in Martinsried in 1984.Hegemann's interest in how the single-celled alga Chlamydomonas senses light led to the discovery of light-gated ion channels. Working with Georg Nagel, he showed that channelrhodopsins could make cells respond directly to light.Georg Nagel, born in Weingarten, Germany, in 1953, is a professor of molecular plant physiology at the department for molecular plant physiology and biophysics – botany I, University of Würzburg. He received his PhD from the University of Frankfurt in 1988.Nagel played a key role in establishing that channelrhodopsins are light-gated ion channels. By introducing the algal genes into frog egg cells, he and Hegemann demonstrated that the proteins could turn light into an electrical signal in other cells, providing the crucial foundation for the later development of optogenetics.
Article Summary: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Their work has enabled researchers to switch individual nerve cells on or off in living brains, helping them study how neural circuits control memories, feelings and behaviours.

India head coach Gautam Gambhir has opened up about his conversations with teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and explained why the youngster had to wait for his chance despite being in good form.Sooryavanshi made history earlier this year when he became the youngest Indian to play international cricket. He made his T20I debut against England at the age of 15 years and 99 days, breaking Sachin Tendulkar’s long-standing record.He then became the youngest player to score a half-century in men’s international cricket when he reached the milestone against Zimbabwe at 15 years and 118 days.Despite his early success, Sooryavanshi did not get a game during the entire Afghanistan series or the one-off T20I against Japan ahead of the Asian Games The 15-year-old returned to the India XI in the Asian Games semifinal against Sri Lanka. He made a bigger contribution in the game, scoring 38 off 21 balls.Gambhir said he had explained to Sooryavanshi that being in good form does not always mean a player will immediately get an opportunity."It was a new experience for me as well. Yes, he was in good form, but I made him understand that sometimes, because of the players who have done well for a long time, he will have to wait for his opportunity.And there's one more thing, social media or outside noise doesn't decide the playing eleven," Gambhir said on JioStar.Gambhir said the playing XI is picked based on what the coach and captain believe is the best combination to win a match."It depends on who in that dressing room, or who the coach and captain feel can win us the match, or what is the best playing eleven, and who have done well for such a long time. Because if Vaibhav plays today, then it's going to be a tough conversation between me and whoever we leave out, whether it's Abhishek or Sanju."So, we can't suddenly ignore a combination that has created such an impact over the last one and a half or two years, and after three or four failures, drop them and play a young player who is very talented, who is also in very good form. So, sometimes you will have to wait for your opportunity because we want to create that security in that dressing room," he added.Sooryavanshi also played a part in India’s successful Asian Games title defence. He scored a quick 15 off nine balls in the final as India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to retain the gold medal.At 15 years, six months and six days, Sooryavanshi also became the youngest Indian to win an Asian Games gold medal.He surpassed shooter Saurabh Chaudhary , who was 16 years, three months and nine days old when he won the men’s 10m air pistol gold medal at the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta.

NEW DELHI: India batter KL Rahul says he is working on improving his game against the old ball so that he can help the team score more runs in the middle overs.Rahul spoke to JioStar after scoring 129 off 87 balls in the third ODI against West Indies. India posted 351, but the total was not enough as the visitors chased it down in 48.2 overs.India had already won the series after taking the first two games.Rahul said batting in the final 10 overs becomes difficult when the ball gets old and starts to reverse swing."It's not been easy to get 80-90 in the last 10 overs. The ball's been getting reverse swing, and even in this game, once the ball got old and soft, and started to reverse swing, as a batter you don't feel confident enough to take on the long-on and deep mid-wicket fielder if it's a big boundary on that side," he said.Rahul said he is now working on finding ways to attack the older ball, especially because he naturally prefers facing a harder ball."...I like the hard ball coming onto me, I can use the pace. So that's something I've been working on, trying to play with softer, older balls and being able to hit sixes with that."I constantly try to get better within my own game, understand my role, understand what a number five and number six batter has to do to consistently put up performances for the team," he added.Rahul also spoke about India’s preparations for the ODI World Cup in South Africa next year.With teams regularly chasing big totals, Rahul said 340 or 350 is no longer always a safe score. He believes India’s middle order must find ways to score faster and push the team towards 370 or 380.West Indies chased 352 in 48.2 overs in the third ODI. India had also chased a record 406 in the second ODI in Guwahati, completing the chase in just 43.2 overs."We don't want to go too far away from the plan but also experiment a little bit as a batting unit. The goal so far has been about can we score 330-340 while batting first, but we're seeing that 340s and 350s get chased down very easily in one-day cricket," he said."So how can batters, once set, keep pressing on and get 370s and 380s, or push for 400 on a given day. The minute we as middle-order batters go in, the aim is to ensure that we do not take too much time to get going and start rotating the strike and keep hitting a boundary every six or seven balls."The coach and captain have been very clear on the personnel they want to bring in. They want to give a longer rope to certain players who we feel might be important for the World Cup," he explained.Rahul has been batting at No. 5 or No. 6 for some time. He said his 129 against West Indies was important because it allowed him to spend a long time at the crease and test the changes he has been making to his batting."I wanted to spend more time with the bat out there in the middle and the last time I really got to bat for a long duration in ODI cricket, in the middle-order was in early January this year against New Zealand, and since then I haven't really got a lot of time to play a long innings."And next year is a big one, with the World Cup starting in October, so it's important for me to get valuable batting time because off the field I'm trying a few things and I want to test that in the game."And only then will you know whether the work that you're putting behind the scenes is working or not, or what I need to do differently. So yeah, it was important for me to get some batting time," he said.
Article Summary: KL Rahul says he is working on improving his game against the old ball. India batsman scored 129 off 87 balls in the third ODI against West Indies. India posted 351, but the visitors chased it down in 48.2 overs.

Article Title: NBA injury update: Spurs coach drops latest status on $31 million forward ahead of NBA season opener
Article Text:

Tobias Harris injury update : Spurs coach says there is no rush on the calf strain

How the Spurs lineup could look without him

Tobias Harris' injury update from San Antonio came with no timetable attached. Coach Mitch Johnson told reporters Sunday that the Spurs will let a left calf strain heal at its own pace, even with the season opener against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Oct. 20 getting close.San Antonio signed Harris this offseason to share the frontcourt with Victor Wembanyama, and his first camp has been interrupted by a strain with no firm return date. The $31 million forward sat out the weekend scrimmage and will be checked again once the preseason wraps up.Tobias Harris, 34, strained a left calf muscle in training camp, and the Spurs made the news public Sunday. The team lists Harris as questionable for the Oct. 20 opener and says a fresh evaluation will come after the preseason. Roughly two weeks separate the announcement from opening night.The Spurs announced the strain, Tom Orsborn of the San Antonio Express-News reported that Harris would not suit up for the scrimmage, and Johnson addressed it afterward at Frost Bank Center, "We won't rush him at all."The coach added that the staff sees no cause for alarm at this level of seriousness, though he stopped short of rating the strain.Asked about the opener, Johnson said Harris' availability is very much in doubt and the team will not push him toward that game. San Antonio has not given a return date or a number of weeks, so the next real update comes when Harris is reevaluated after the preseason, which opens Oct. 8 at home against the Atlanta Hawks and runs five games.The 6-foot-8 forward is not an easy piece to replace. Harris spent the past two seasons in Detroit, and last year the Pistons won 60 games and finished first in the East while Harris averaged 13.3 points, 5.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists over 63 appearances. Harris also shot 46.9% from the field and 36.8% from three in 27.7 minutes a night.San Antonio saw a big offseason pickup in those numbers. The idea was to add veteran presence and versatility to a team coming off a historic run to the 2026 NBA Finals. Harris was projected as the main frontcourt partner for Wembanyama, and the two-year, $31 million contract makes this more than a depth issue. Harris lists at small forward and power forward, so the injury touches more than one spot in the rotation.Without Harris, the Spurs will likely turn to the group that carried them last year, including Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell and Julian Champagnie, with Dylan Harper coming off the bench. Carter Bryant, Harrison Barnes and Keldon Johnson give the staff extra options while Harris heals.

Article Title: The road to LA 2028: How Sjoerd Marijne and his team rebuilt India's women's hockey side
Article Text:
Image credit: Hockey India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

At the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium, tears flowed freely on the pitch. More than 5,500km away, in India, women’s hockey’s loyal legion, small in numbers but deep in investment, rejoiced.They had watched a team in which skill was matched by fitness, individual brilliance was backed by teamwork and, finally, belief had returned.The gold medal, won after 44 years, was defining. But the direct ticket to the Los Angeles Olympics was unprecedented.Interest in women’s hockey had gathered pace after India’s fourth-place finish at the Tokyo Olympics. Missing out on Paris, however, dented the hopes and aspirations that had begun to build.Then came the well-documented rifts, allegations, a dip in form and a spate of injuries. The shadow over Los Angeles grew darker.Enter Sjoerd Marijne and his support staff. They did not have a magic wand to make the demons disappear. What they brought was a systematic approach to rebuilding the physical and psychological framework of the team.The Dutchman was quick to point out that rebuilding a team is never the work of one person.“There’s a great connection among the staff and the players. I’m doing the interviews, but it’s an achievement from the whole staff. I’m really happy with all the quality I have around me,” he said.But there was another requirement, ensuring the players were fit enough to play as one.That was where Wayne Lombard, the team’s head of athletic performance, came in. He had a broad idea of the physical state of the squad when he arrived.The support staff hit the reset button. Rodet Yila and Caira Yila were brought in as scientific advisers, while the immediate priority was not fitness for fitness’ sake, but getting the players healthy.“Regardless of what the fitness levels were, the priority was to address the injury concerns,” Lombard said.That required more than exercises and numbers. The players had to believe in the process.“We had to sit down with the players and earn their buy-in. Helping them understand that the physical side of the game is every bit as important as the technical and tactical side,” Lombard said.He introduced the 30-15 intermittent fitness test to establish the players’ maximum aerobic speed. The test required them to run for 30 seconds, rest for 15 and progress across a 40m grid, with the speed increasing by 0.5kmph at every stage.Muscle by muscle, the players rebuilt their strength. With it came confidence.As the year progressed, India began to look increasingly like a team t rather than a collection of talented individuals.Poetic justice or coincidence, Japan had stood in India’s way in the qualifiers for the Paris Olympics. In Japan, a little over two years later, India cleared the hurdle to Los Angeles.
Article Summary: The gold medal, won after 44 years, was defining. But the direct ticket to the Los Angeles Olympics was unprecedented. Sjoerd Marijne and his support staff brought a systematic approach to rebuilding the physical and psychological framework of the team.

Article Title: Woman convicted of killing 10-year-old held in Delhi after 20 years in hiding
Article Text:
She changed her name to Pooja and moved through different places to avoid detection. (AI Image)





NEW DELHI: For more than 20 years, Sadhana managed to live away from prison where she was to serve a life sentence. A life convict in a kidnapping-murder case of a 10-year-old boy, Sadhana went missing after walking out on parole in Dec 2005.Over the years, police said, she changed her name, moved cities and built a new life as Pooja. Last week, Delhi Police ’s crime branch arrested her in Haridwar.The case dates back to Jan 6, 1990, when the boy went missing from Azadpur T-point. Police said witnesses Jagdish Chand and Vasdev had seen Sadhana holding his hand while crossing GT Road around 5.30pm. Sadhana and co-accused Raj Kumar were arrested from Jahangirpuri.The two were living together and the child’s father, Balwant Ram, and his family had objected to it. A previous dispute led to resentment and a decision to take revenge, police said.During the trial, Sadhana was found to be the last person seen with the child. Police said she had also concealed Kumar’s presence at her house and played an active role in the conspiracy. She was convicted under sections 302 (murder), 364 (kidnapping or abducting in order to murder) and 120B (criminal conspiracy) of IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment.Sadhana was lodged in Tihar Jail on Jan 9, 1990.After spending years in jail, Sadhana was released on parole on Dec 27, 2005, which was extended by three weeks on medical grounds. She, however, did not surrender on Jan 18, 2006, and began a second life.She changed her name to Pooja and moved through different places to avoid detection. Police said her final parole was arranged by another Raj Kumar, a Tilak Nagar resident, on the reference of Janki, a woman who was lodged with Sadhana in jail. Sadhana stayed with him before taking up a job at a private company in Noida.There, she met Keshav, a carpenter. They moved to Mukundpur, where they lived for around five years before shifting to Haridwar. Police said Sadhana married Keshav in a temple and used his name as her husband in documents, helping conceal her identity.Meanwhile, investigators continued to pursue leads through intelligence, old associates and family links. A recent lead about a woman living under an assumed identity took a team to Haridwar and Sadhana was arrested on Sept 27. Her years of borrowed independence came to an end as she was sent back to jail.

India are currently fifth in the overall medal standings.India’s medal tally received a major boost over the last two days, with the contingent adding gold medals across boxing, wrestling, archery, hockey and golf. Lovlina Borgohain, Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal, Sujeet Kalkal, the Indian women’s hockey team, Kumkum Mohod and Pranavi Urs have all contributed gold medals to India’s latest surge.Kumkum also won silver alongside Dhiraj Bommadevara in the mixed recurve team event, while India’s women’s golf team of Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar secured silver.On October 3, Kumkum Mohod added another gold by winning the women’s individual recurve event. The 17-year-old defeated South Korea’s Oh Yejin 6-5 in a shoot-off to become the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games. Her victory also secured an Olympic quota place for India for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.Pranavi Urs also scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to win individual golf gold at the Asian Games, while helping India claim silver in the women’s team event alongside Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar.India’s women’s cricket team won the country’s first gold medal of the Games after defeating Sri Lanka in the final. Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet then added India’s second gold by winning the 10m air pistol mixed team event.India subsequently won both the men’s and women’s kabaddi titles, while Neeru Dhanda secured gold in the women’s trap event. She later teamed up with Kynan Chenai to win the mixed trap team gold.In athletics, Kiran Pahal, Poovamma Machettira, Prachi Choudhary and Vithya Ramraj won gold in the women’s 4x400m relay. India also dominated the compound archery events, winning gold in the men’s team, women’s team and mixed team events.On October 2, Lovlina Borgohain defeated China’s Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the women’s 75kg final to win gold. The victory came on her birthday and made Lovlina only the second Indian woman boxer after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games gold.The women’s recurve team of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod then created history by defeating South Korea 5-3 to win India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the event.India then added three more gold medals in boxing and wrestling, with Parveen Hooda winning the women’s 65kg title, Ankush Panghal taking gold in the men’s 80kg category and Sujeet Kalkal winning the men’s freestyle 65kg event.The Indian women’s hockey team ended a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold by defeating China 1-0 in the final, with the victory also securing a direct qualification spot for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.On October 3, Kumkum completed a memorable Asian Games campaign by winning individual recurve gold. After being pushed to a shoot-off by Oh Yejin, the 17-year-old held her nerve to shoot a 10 and beat the South Korean 8, securing India’s first individual women’s recurve gold at the Asian Games.Pranavi Urs added another historic gold in golf. The 23-year-old became the first Indian woman to win an individual golf gold medal at the Asian Games. She also helped India win silver in the women’s team event.India’s silver medal haul has come across shooting, athletics, weightlifting, wushu, squash, wrestling, sailing, archery and golf.The shooting contingent has been one of India’s biggest contributors, with medals across air rifle, 50m rifle 3 positions, 25m pistol and trap events.Mirabai Chanu ended her long wait for an Asian Games medal by taking silver in the women’s 49kg weightlifting event, while Roshibina Devi won silver in women’s 60kg sanda. Gulveer Singh also enjoyed a strong Games, winning silver in the men’s 10,000m and 1500m events.In squash, Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh won silver in the women’s and men’s singles events respectively. India also collected silver medals in sailing and archery, with Prince Noble Kurisinkal and Manu Francis finishing second in the men’s skiff.Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara lost to China in the mixed recurve final, while Dhiraj Bommadevara, Neeraj Chauhan and Yashdeep Bhoge finished runners-up to South Korea in the men’s recurve team event.The latest addition came in golf, where Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar won silver in the women’s team event. China took gold, while India finished second.India’s bronze medals have come from a wide range of disciplines, including shooting, athletics, squash, boxing, wrestling, archery, sailing, sepaktakraw, badminton, rowing, table tennis, kurash, soft tennis and mixed martial arts.Athletics has produced a large share of India’s bronze medals, with Parul Chaudhary, Gulveer Singh, Tejaswin Shankar, Vithya Ramraj, Pooja Singh, Rohit Yadav and others contributing to the tally.India’s squash contingent has also produced multiple medals, with Joshna Chinappa, Velavan Senthilkumar, Anahat Singh, Tanvi Khanna, Abhay Singh and Veer Chotrani contributing across the mixed doubles and team events.In boxing, Narender Berwal, Priya Ghanghas and Kapil Pokhariya won bronze, while Sunil Kumar secured bronze in Greco-Roman wrestling.Nethra Kumanan won bronze in the women’s dinghy sailing event, while India’s men’s quadrant team secured bronze in sepaktakraw after losing 0-2 to Japan in the semifinal.

Article Title: 'He was amazed and bewildered’: Man behind Delhi Metro voice Shammi Narang takes grandson on first ride
Article Text:
The video ended with Narang recreating the familiar announcement for Sultanpur station, giving the family outing an especially personal touch.





NEW DELHI: For years, Shammi Narang’s voice has been a familiar sound for Delhi Metro commuters. But a recent journey turned into a memorable family moment when his young grandson heard that voice over the Metro’s announcement system for the first time.Narang, a former national news anchor with Doordarshan, recently took his grandson Rushaan on his first-ever ride on the Delhi Metro and shared a video of the experience on X."I may not travel on these Metro trains forever… but I take immense pride in knowing that my voice will travel from one generation to another. From me to my little grandson, Rushaan, and perhaps one day to his grandchildren… and beyond, " Shammi Narang tweeted."Today, we took Rushaan on his very first Metro ride. He was equal parts amazed and bewildered to hear Dadu’s voice echoing through the train… a voice he knows, but in a place he had never heard it before. A rather special moment for us, " Shammi added in a post.The child appeared surprised as the announcements began playing inside the train, eventually recognising the voice as that of his grandfather.Narang was seen holding Rushaan during the journey while the child’s parents encouraged him to identify the familiar voice.For Rushaan, however, the experience was less about the legacy behind the voice and more about the surprise of hearing his grandfather speak from the Metro’s announcement system.The family appeared to enjoy the moment as Rushaan gradually connected the voice he knew at home with the announcements playing inside the train.The video ended with Narang recreating the familiar announcement for Sultanpur station, giving the family outing an especially personal touch.
